newsitem.title: USA: Clinton "quite optimistic" about tax cut package.
newsitem.headline: Clinton "quite optimistic" about tax cut package.

text.p: President Clinton said Friday he was "quite optimistic" that the White House and Congress would reach agreement on a tax cut package in spite of the partisan skirimishing now underway.

"I'm frankly quite optimistic. You would expect that all the parties would advance their views in the most vigorous way possible," Clinton said at a White House ceremony. He was to spell out his position on a final tax package on Monday.
Earlier in the day, the White House reiterated that the House-passed tax cut bill and a version headed toward Senate passage were unacceptable to Clinton in their present form.
"The President wants a tax cut. He wants a targeted tax cut, and the House and Senate measures don't quite muster up at this point," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

"We should expect a little of this skirmishing. We're going to offer our thoughts on Monday," Clinton said, adding that the final package should help families raise their children and help fund better education.

Opposition Republicans drafted both the House and Senate tax cut bills but they are not identical and will have to be compromised by a congressional conference committee. McCurry said the White House would make the case for its preferences during the legislative tailoring process, and added that "We think we've got a considerable influence yet to be brought to the table."
